source: CAMFAD student thesis: "Establishment of a New Coconut Plantation Farm", National School of Agriculture, July 1994. Note: this forecast table is scaled to a hypothetical 10,000-hectare coconut development area, distinct from the ~10-12 hectare pilot farm site described elsewhere in the same thesis (see coconut/plantation_site_location) -- the thesis appears to use the pilot site to plan the initial farm build-out, then separately models a much larger-scale national development scenario for this profitability forecast. Digit-level figures are reported as best-effort readings from a dense scanned table and should be treated as approximate.
text:
The thesis models expected coconut yield as roughly 5 to 25 bunches per hectare per year (the source's own stated range), and uses the midpoint of that range, about 15 bunches per hectare per year, as its planning average. Applying an assumed per-bunch weight, this midpoint yield is converted to roughly 3,750 kg (about 3.75 tons) of coconut per hectare per year. At an assumed market price of roughly USD 430 per ton, this gives an estimated annual revenue of roughly USD 1,600 per hectare once the planting reaches this yield level.

Scaled up to a 10,000-hectare development area, the thesis's 10-year profit-and-loss table (covering harvest years in the mid-to-late 1990s, i.e. after the several-year establishment period) shows total revenue received over the 10-year forecast period of roughly USD 80.6 million, total costs of roughly USD 23.9 million, and a resulting projected net profit of roughly USD 56.7 million over the 10 years. The thesis is explicit that this profit projection is not guaranteed and depends heavily on management quality, and frames it as an illustrative planning example rather than a firm commitment, noting that coconut's 25-30 year productive lifespan gives room for yield and price to potentially improve over that horizon.
